commits.message:
feat(config): every config write names its layer, and save offers each layer the session can write (#776)

* docs(spec): a pane's acts go one at a time, and only a restart refuses a slash line (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

* feat(config): the chain is user < project < local, and the local file sits beside the project's under its approval (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.u2t)

* feat(config): every config write names its layer, and save offers each layer the session can write (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.u2t)

An action that writes config takes `layer: user | project | local`
(default user); save also takes `ask`, its default, which binds the role
as the link's value so every click carries a concrete role. Each config
verb's wire carries the role after the session id, and the host refuses a
role the session's chain holds no layer for (no approved project, or an
explicit --config path). The payload says which layers the session can
write, and the bundled save draws a link per writable layer. A local file
the host creates is named in the repository's common info/exclude in the
same landing, so git never sees it.

A save drawn without a layer to bind is now a render error.

* fix(config): a write looks through what its file inherits from the layers beneath it (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.u2t)

A write's by-name reads (the row a placement sits in, the preset a save
copies, a declaration a pin needs, the names a new preset avoids) read the
bundled default as if it were all the written file inherits. Over a user
file, a project or local write refused placements the user's rows held,
copied a bundled row over the user's own, missed presets the user declared
and could mint a name the user's file held. They now read the loader's merge
of the layers beneath the file, which the chain load already runs before its
validation and now offers on its own; a root lowered from a tree is copied
whole, since its positional rows have no name a file can write under.

The lane handoff's button is the way out of a lane, so it resets the switch
in every layer the session can write; the menu's ↺ stays the user layer's.

Also: every role's write is projected from one resolution; the exclude entry
is escaped for gitignore and matched as git reads a line; the project's
config base names live in one table; comments, law markers and the save docs
the reviews named.

* fix(config): a click's writes are proved against the files as the click leaves them (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.u2t)

A click can write more than one layer (a `do` across layers, the lane
escape, an undo step), and each write was proved against the other layers as
they stood on disk: a value an earlier write of the same click set in the
project's file did not hide a later user write of the same field. A write's
neighbouring layers are now every role's file location, read through the
click, and an undo or redo step proves each file between the others as the
step leaves them. A layer beneath that does not load refuses the write,
naming why.

A bare `save` writes the user's layer, as every other config write does, so
it never throws at render; `layer: "ask"` binds the layer per link. The lane
escape resets its switches in this person's own layers, never the project's
checked-in file. Refusal messages, verb docs and comments say what the
layers now are.

* docs(config): a bare save writes the user layer (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.u2t)
